description: the man of the reference picture riding: an ancient forest god, an old man with weathered light skin, a long grey beard and long grey hair, a kind wise face in clean profile, eyes glowing green, a great crown of branching brown antlers with small green leaves and white blossoms, a long pale grey robe like birch bark with a green sash, a long cloak of living green vines and moss with small pink and white flowers hanging behind from the shoulders, the robe hanging down along the leg, a brown leather shoe, no staff, no tree of light and nothing in the hands but the reins; sitting tall and upright astride a saddle that is not drawn, the back straight, not squatting and not crouching, seen exactly from the side in a strict profile, facing right, the head, chest and hips turned fully to the right; both forearms reaching forward, the two hands together in front of the body holding short reins that end just in front of the hands; only the near leg showing and only one foot in the whole picture: the thigh lying forward and level from the hip to the knee, the knee bent at a right angle, the lower leg hanging vertically straight down from the knee, one whole foot at the bottom with the toes pointing right; the cloak and any long hair hanging down behind the back, not spread out; the far leg completely hidden and not drawn at all, no second boot and no second foot; the whole figure from the tips of the antlers to the sole of the foot inside the picture with room around it; nothing under the rider; isolated figure on a plain background

references.usage: the character's look: this same man, his face, hair, beard, antler crown, robe, vine cloak and colours, drawn the same way; not his standing pose and not the blossoming staff and the tree of light
